label: Early original-phase position (mostly 3rd input token), token-modulated
explanation: Fires only in the original input phase, at steps t=1..3. It never fires at t=0, at t>=4, at the delimiter, or during copy (14 of 64k dev activations are outside t=1..3). t=2 (the third original token) holds 78% of activation mass, with about 41% of t=2 steps active; t=1 holds 15% and t=3 holds 8%. Within this window the token content decides whether it fires and how strongly. Current inputs f, j, i, c and 1 raise the rate (f is 3.3x). So do earlier tokens b and f, as the first token or the previous token. The strongest examples are sequences like b b f / b f f, where an f arrives at step 2 after b. It mostly fires on the first occurrence of a token (in_first=1 holds 92% of mass). The window alone (t in 1..3) gives recall about 1.0 but precision 0.21. The chosen predicate covers t=2 plus the high-lift input tokens at t=1 and t=3. It gets dev F1 0.54 and mass recall 0.91. Precision is limited because the exact token dependence was not captured by a simple rule.
